newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher, buoyed by land auction.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher, buoyed by land auction.

text.p: Tokyo stocks finished Tuesday's session higher but well off earlier gains of three percent.
Brokers said short-covering of futures, by dealers especially, was inspired by the surprisingly good results of an auction on Monday of land in central Tokyo.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended 228.38 points or 1.26 percent higher at 18,314.33. Its March futures added 200 to end at 18,340.
"Sentiment improved greatly, thanks to the land auction results, which were much better than expected," a strategist at a medium-sized brokerage said.

"The market hopes a recovery in land prices will spur the economy and breathe life into the problem loan-laden banking and construction sectors -- all factors which would prop up stocks as a whole," he added.
